text.p: Spain on Thursday blocked an agreement between the European Union and Jordan in anger at the size of Jordan's tomato paste quota, threatening the progress of the bloc's whole Mediterranean policy, EU diplomats said.

The association agreement was part of a series being concluded with 12 Mediterranean countries to create an eventual free trade zone in the region. Four accords have been reached so far and talks are also under way with Egypt and Lebanon.

Jordan had initialled the agreement on April 16 on the sidelines of the European-Mediterranean conference in Malta, but Spain is now objecting that the amount of tomato paste Jordan would be able to export under the deal is too large.
Diplomats said Spain's action was part of a growing muscle-flexing process ahead of changes in the EU's aid programme for its poorest members.
"Spain is beginning to become a problem in the European Union," one diplomat said at a meeting of EU foreign affairs ministers in Luxembourg.
EU aid programmes are due for an overhaul over the next few years as the bloc takes in countries from the former Communist eastern Europe.

Spain's veto for now of the tomata paste clause means the whole agreement could have to be renegotiated, as Jordan has indicated that if the negotiation were to be reopened formally, it would seek changes on a range of points.
